PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds revealed in
earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only tells you how often this line type was paid at all.
- If you decide the line is indemnified and no cap, sub-limit or percentage reduction applies,
  take the stated amount as t and give a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. These
  amounts are before such policy arithmetic; apply caps and reductions on top.
- A line type that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies
  do not carry; price it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.

items.rationale: Like-for-like fittings for the failed heating-pipe joint are covered under §§2.4.3(a) and 7.1.7(c). Four elbows at €10.50 each is €42, subject to documented use.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(c), (e) require evidence that this second set was needed and is not a duplicate. If supported, four elbows at €10.50 each is €42.

Section 7.1.8(e) requires the size and quantity to match the localized repair; the account does not establish why five 28 mm elbows were needed. If documented, the five-piece reference estimate is €104.
Five additional large elbows are not supported by the one-metre repair account under §§7.1.5 and 7.1.8(e). If shown to be necessary, the five-piece reference estimate is €103.
A single offset fitting could be part of the reconnection, but §7.1.8(e) requires confirmation that the 28 mm size was used on the affected section. The comparable single fitting is €21.
Necessary fixings are covered under §7.1.7(c). Eight screws at €1.16 each is about €9.30.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary supports, but §7.1.8(e) requires confirmation that the 10 mm size matches the repair. Four clamps at €4.80 each is €19.20.
Supports sized for the listed 15 mm copper pipe are covered under §7.1.7(c) if used on the affected section. Four at about €5.25 each is €21.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary labour at customary rates. The reported time on site supports this block; 6.75 hours at about €92 per hour is approximately €619.
The claim confirms that a helper assisted for part of the repair, covered under §7.1.7(g). The reference estimate for 5.75 hours is €409.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(e) limit the allowance to the approximately one metre actually replaced, not the 6.4 m billed. At €15.40 per metre, the supported allowance is €15.40.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel charge for this contractor and invoice. The comparable gross charge is €80.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers repair consumables that are not already itemized. The comparable flat charge is €43.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes separate processing charges. The positive amount is a conditional estimate only, not an allowance.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers like-for-like insulation on the repaired section. With only about one metre documented, the supported allowance is one metre at €23 rather than six metres.

Sections 7.1.8(c) and (e) bar duplicate or unsupported insulation, and the account does not identify separate matting beyond the pipe insulation. If a distinct mat were shown to be necessary, allow about €20 for the localized section.
Binding wire used to secure the replacement insulation qualifies under §7.1.7(c). Two units at about €13 each gives €26, subject to the quantity being tied to the repair.

The reported day and a half on site makes a second labour block plausible under §7.1.7(g), provided it is distinct from the first and attributable to covered work. The reference estimate for seven hours is €642.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows only one travel charge per contractor per invoice, so line 12 takes precedence. The €80 estimate is conditional only.

Section 7.1.8(b) excludes contractor protective equipment, and the bundle does not separately identify any eligible repair consumables. A separately supported consumables allowance would be about €12.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover necessary disposal of the removed pipe and insulation. Comparable small repair-waste charges support €60 gross.

Localized cleanup may qualify under §§5.2.1 and 7.1.8(a), but the combined line includes an undocumented coating that is not shown to restore a pre-loss finish under §§7.1.5 and 7.1.9. If the eligible cleanup can be separated, allow about €110 rather than five hours for the full treatment.
